dedupe_keys.name: network rail earthworks asset management 190 000 cuttings and embankments

description: Network Rail manages the infrastructure slopes that carry 20,000 miles of track in Great Britain: a portfolio of more than 190,000 earthwork assets made up of embankments, soil cuttings and rock cuttings. Its page says most slopes are over 150 years old and lack the capability and resilience of modern engineered slopes, and that they often show vulnerability after prolonged wet weather or heavy rain, leading to landslips. The company uses a risk-based policy to target maintenance of drainage and vegetation and capital investment to strengthen slopes, with specialist geotechnical engineers using examination and monitoring data, and it published an earthworks technical strategy in June 2018; it is a founding member of the UK Geotechnical Asset Owners' Forum. Coverage: the British rail network. Format and access: a public web page. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: the asset data themselves are not published on this page. It supports hazard exposure, resilience and climate adaptation studies of ageing rail earthworks. It relates to the Network Rail WRCCA plans, the drainage allowances case and the Carmont derailment in the catalogue.
